concept: One player is a printed lock; the others are picking it with their hands, not with logic tokens. The Locksmith loads five hidden pin stacks into a cylinder behind a shroud; challengers set the sliders on their own key blanks, insert, and turn — the plug rotates exactly as far as their first wrong chamber, and stops. Audience: deduction players who liked Mastermind-style feedback but are sick of a rival reading it off a card. Emotion: held-breath tension, paid off by a physical click nobody can dispute. Piggyback: guess-and-feedback deduction, turn order. Scoring: each challenger who opens the lock scores the round's remaining time-value; the Locksmith scores 1 per failed turn, and the seat rotates every round, so nobody is the referee for long. 2 players = alternating legs, best of four.
mechanism: A print-in-place cylinder whose five chambers are sequential gates on a staircase cam: the plug can only pass gate 2 if gate 1 is already correct, so rotation angle on the printed protractor window publicly reports how many chambers are right IN ORDER — the one signal, physically generated, impossible to fudge. Pins come from a ladder of heights 3.0–6.0 mm in 0.4 mm steps; key blanks carry five detented sliders on the same ladder. After each failed turn the Locksmith may re-pin exactly ONE chamber — the act is public, the choice is secret — so old knowledge rots and the crackers must decide whether to spend a turn re-testing a chamber they already 'know'. Fun-correct bet: the winning line is reading bind order and spending turns to isolate a single chamber; brute-force slider guessing runs out of turns because the feedback is ordinal, not per-chamber. Nearest known: Mastermind, Turing Machine (2022), Black Box.
physical_hook: Cardboard breaks: the feedback is mechanical binding — a paper version needs a lookup table and a trusted human reading it, which is exactly the referee the shroud exists to delete. Molding breaks: the whole game is a 0.4 mm tolerance ladder plus print-in-place key sliders and a per-copy pin assortment, and a mold locks one fixed catalog with a parting seam through the shear line.
title: Re-Pin
